defect: A database recording error propagates out of record_activity_stream; that future participates in the API server select, so a transient SQLite write failure terminates the whole server.
fact: Any Err from hel::hel_database::record_api_activities (src/hel_database/events.rs:179, which returns rusqlite errors from a write transaction at line 193 onward) is propagated by `??` at mj-cli/src/server/api_activity.rs:45 out of the loop in record_activity_stream. That future is an arm of the tokio::select! at mj-cli/src/server.rs:2021. When any arm completes, the select ends, the serve (server.rs:852) and control (server.rs:856) futures are dropped, and run_server returns the error at server.rs:2036. So one failed activity write stops the whole API server.
query: Which error returns inside the new code reach the end of run_server, and by what route? In particular, which select! arms end the server when they return Err, and which fallible calls feed each arm?
tool_output: Annotation on server.rs:2021: "This select! arm ends run_server when it completes. record_activity_stream completes with Err whenever record_api_activities (events.rs:179, a SQLite write) fails, through `??` at api_activity.rs:45. Its normal (Ok) exit is only when the snapshot sender closes. Result: one database write error drops serve and control and stops the server."
specificity_reason: Error propagation by `?` is everywhere, so a plain list of error routes would be low specificity. The useful output is narrower: errors from a fallible I/O call inside a long-running background loop end a top-level server select!. A typical diff adds few such arms, and here the arm sits next to serve and control. Still, the tool cannot tell whether ending the server is intended, as it is for the serve and control arms. A reviewer would have to judge that, so the output is not as decisive as a self-lock or a branch that can never run.
evidence: git show efbd4bc08: mj-cli/src/server/api_activity.rs:8-51 (new file). The loop calls spawn_blocking(record_api_activities) at lines 38-45 and ends in `.context("API activity recorder task failed")??;`. It returns Ok only when snapshots.changed() fails (lines 47-49). mj-cli/src/server.rs:2020-2024 adds `result = api_activity::record_activity_stream(activity_snapshots) => result.context("native API activity recorder stopped")` beside the `serve => result` and `control => result` arms. server.rs:2036 is `result?;`. src/hel_database/events.rs:179-193: record_api_activities submits a write that opens connection.transaction() and reads before it writes. Fix 3c668c3d9: its commit message says the recorder "was also an arm of the server's select, so its first failure ended the server". The fix moves the recorder into its own task with retry, and makes writer transactions IMMEDIATE. The whole route is visible in the diff. The SQLITE_BUSY trigger depends on SQLite behavior outside the repository, but you do not need it to see that any write error stops the server.

defect: At phone widths with an empty composer, Tab from the editor into Send/Attach removes composer-has-intent and hides the toolbar holding the newly focused button.
fact: When focus moves to #send-button (viewer.html:222) or #attach-image, the focusin listener (viewer.js:7539) and the focusout branch for a relatedTarget inside the form (viewer.js:7541-7543) call syncComposerLayout. There, document.activeElement is not promptText, so editorFocused is false (viewer.js:5824). With an empty composer and no images, the predicate at viewer.js:5828-5830 is false, so composer-has-intent is removed. Under max-width 640px, viewer.css:2196-2198 then sets display:none on .composer-actions (viewer.html:221), which is an ancestor of the element that has just received focus. The handler hides the element it was called for.
query: For each focus event that calls syncComposerLayout, which values can editorFocused and the composer-has-intent predicate take when the focus target is a button inside .composer-actions? Does the resulting class state match a CSS rule that hides an ancestor of that focused element?
tool_output: Warning at viewer.js:7539 (focusin -> syncComposerLayout): when focus lands on #send-button or #attach-image (inside #composer-actions, viewer.html:221), the handler computes editorFocused=false (viewer.js:5824). If hasText and hasAttachments are false and composerActionPointerDown is false (keyboard focus), it removes 'composer-has-intent'. Under @media (max-width: 640px), viewer.css:2196 '#prompt-form .composer-actions {display:none}' then applies to an ancestor of the focused element, so the focused element becomes hidden. The only exemption, composerActionPointerDown (viewer.js:7552), is set only by pointerdown.
specificity_reason: A finding that a focus handler hides the element receiving focus, or its container, is rare and is almost always a bug. Its output would point at this one listener and CSS rule, not at many harmless places. The analysis needs to work across JS, CSS and HTML, including media queries, which is unusual for a static tool. But the fact itself is narrow and names the defect directly, including the keyboard case not covered by the pointer-only exemption.
evidence: At 0cb5bc6665: viewer.js:5820-5836: composerActionPointerDown and syncComposerLayout, with predicate editorFocused || hasText || hasAttachments || composerActionPointerDown, where editorFocused = document.activeElement === promptText. viewer.js:7539: focusin calls syncComposerLayout. viewer.js:7540-7546: focusout calls it synchronously when relatedTarget is inside promptForm. viewer.js:7547-7560: the exemption is set only on pointerdown and pointerup. viewer.js:5806-5818: syncSendButtonDisabled does not check text, so Send is enabled and tabbable when the composer is empty. viewer.css:2196-2202 (inside the phone media query): .composer-actions is display:none unless composer-has-intent is set. viewer.html:221-222: #composer-actions contains #send-button. viewer.js:5985: attach-image is shown when images are supported. All of these lines are in the diff, so the defect is visible there. A tool would still add value by stating the combined consequence across the three files.

defect: Worker recovery and parked sub-agent wake compare the digest of the image worker (through the hel link) with the host worker, which differs in bytes, and copy the host worker over the link.
fact: The commit adds a second way to write the session's installed worker path `{worker_root}/hel`: install.rs:701 and install.rs:790-797 (WorkerInstall::Image) make it a symlink to IMAGE_WORKER (`ln -sfn`). Other code that reads and writes that same path was left unchanged and still assumes it holds a copy of the host binary. worker_binary_refresh_plan (upgrade.rs:721-726) hashes `{worker_root}/hel` with sha256sum, which follows the link. replace_target_worker_binary_if_stale (upgrade.rs:789-806) compares that digest with the digest of the host binary from worker_binary_for (upgrade.rs:756). When they differ, installed_worker_binary_replacement_plan (upgrade.rs:505, mv at 564) moves a host copy over the link. So, for an image-linked container, the digest at upgrade.rs:806 is the image worker's digest, which never equals the host binary's digest, and recovery or a parked sub-agent's wake replaces the image link with a host copy.
query: Which other functions read or write the file `{worker_root}/hel` that install_worker_files now may create as a symlink to IMAGE_WORKER, and do they handle WorkerInstall::Image or still take a host binary `&Path`?
tool_output: Note on install.rs:790-797: `{worker_root}/hel` can now be a symlink to IMAGE_WORKER (WorkerInstall::Image). These unchanged sites also use `{worker_root}/hel` and do not consult WorkerInstall: upgrade.rs:726 worker_binary_refresh_plan (sha256sum follows the link), upgrade.rs:806 compares that digest with the digest of worker_binary_for(locator) (the host binary), and upgrade.rs:505/564 installed_worker_binary_replacement_plan (`mv -f` host copy over the path). Callers that reach them: refresh_target_worker_binary_if_stale (session_manager/recovery.rs) and refresh_installed_worker_binary (parked sub-agent wake). Also: provisioning.rs:1149, install.rs:1141, process.rs:162/281, targets/worker_daemon.rs:309.
specificity_reason: The tool would list about nine sites that use the same path. Most only run the worker, and that still works through the link. Only the digest gate and the replacement plan assume a host copy. A reviewer would have to read a short list to find the two that matter. The output is rare in an ordinary diff because few changes alter the kind of file at a shared path, but the list is not limited to the defect. A value-flow version ("the digest at upgrade.rs:806 comes from IMAGE_WORKER and is compared with the host binary's digest") would be more pointed, but the tool must first find the readers of the path. Those references come from formatted strings, not from a shared symbol.
evidence: git show 1035ca69e7: install.rs:701 `let installed = format!("{worker_root}/hel")`, install.rs:790-797 `exec ln -sfn IMAGE_WORKER installed` for WorkerInstall::Image. The diff does not touch upgrade.rs. At intro, upgrade.rs:721-726 worker_binary_refresh_plan uses `{worker_root}/hel` with installed_file_digest_command (upgrade.rs:658-676, `sha256sum -- "$1"`). upgrade.rs:752-766 refresh_target_worker_binary_if_stale resolves the source with worker_binary_for. upgrade.rs:789-806 compares digests with eq_ignore_ascii_case, and on a mismatch runs installed_worker_binary_replacement_plan (upgrade.rs:505, container `mv -f staged installed` at 560-569). `git grep 'worker_root}/hel'` at intro lists provisioning.rs:1149, install.rs:701/1141, process.rs:162/281, upgrade.rs:486/726 and worker_daemon.rs:309. Fix 47edb1ffb says recovery's digest gate "compared the image's worker with the host binary, whose bytes never match even for the same build, and copied the host worker over a current image worker." I agree with the first pass that the diff's ExecPlan observation states the problem and defers it to Milestone 5. The faulty code itself is outside the diff, so a reviewer reading only the code changes would need the tool's list of other users of the path.

defect: The pinned field title is drawn as a single unwrapped row, so a title wider than the pane (or containing a newline) is clipped and its remainder, including a trailing ' (required)', cannot be read anywhere.
fact: The `title` Line built at mj-chat/src/chat/elicitation.rs:1332-1341 holds `field.title` from the agent's request, which has no length limit and may contain newlines. Before the diff, this value reached a Paragraph with `.wrap(Wrap { trim: false })` inside the scrolled body. After the diff, its only rendering sink is `Paragraph::new(title.clone())` at elicitation.rs:1055, which has no `.wrap` and is drawn into `Rect { height: 1, .. }`. `wrapped_height` (elicitation.rs:1310) adds exactly 1 row for it. Any part of the title past the pane width, including the trailing " (required)", is clipped and cannot be scrolled into view.
query: Where is the value built from `field.title` rendered after this change, and does that sink bound its width or height in a way the old sink did not (wrap removed, fixed 1-row area)?
tool_output: elicitation.rs:1055: Unbounded text drawn into a fixed 1-row area without wrapping. `title` contains `field.title` (from ElicitationRequest, no length limit) plus " (required)". It is rendered by `Paragraph::new(title.clone())` with no `.wrap` into `Rect { height: 1 }`. Text wider than `chunks[1].width` is truncated, and the area does not scroll. Before this change the same value was rendered with `Wrap { trim: false }` (old focus body). `wrapped_height` (line 1310) counts it as exactly 1 row.
specificity_reason: A plain lint for "Paragraph without wrap in a 1-row Rect" would fire on many status lines and headers. In this file alone, elicitation.rs:650, 678 and 1251 are also unwrapped Paragraphs. Such a lint would be low specificity. The output above is narrower. It ties the sink to an unbounded value from an external request, and it reports a regression: the same value went from a wrapped sink to an unwrapped, fixed-height one in this diff. That combination is uncommon in an ordinary diff, and a reviewer would read it. It is not rare enough to rate high: clipping can still be an acceptable design choice, so the tool cannot say on its own that this is a bug.
evidence: I read `git show 9651f8c78a`, which changes mj-chat/src/chat/elicitation.rs and its tests, and the file at intro. Line 1055: `Paragraph::new(title.clone())` rendered into `Rect { height: 1, ..chunks[1] }` with no `.wrap`. Lines 1300-1310: `wrapped_height` returns `body.saturating_add(u16::from(self.title.is_some()))`. Lines 1332-1341: `title` is built from `format!("{}{}", field.title, required)`. The diff's removed lines show the earlier body Paragraph using `.wrap(Wrap { trim: false })` with the title as its first line. The commit message says the title is "rendered in its own pinned row", and its live validation used only short titles ("2/4  Enabled"). Every fact needed is in the diff, so I agree with the first pass. A tool would help by putting the dropped wrap together with the fixed height and the unbounded source in one statement.

defect: ReviewDispatch::launch requires a hypothesis for each reviewer and then throws it away, so the specialist prompt never contains the risk it was launched to check.
fact: At intro, the new field `ReviewSubagentRequest::hypothesis` (src/discrete_review.rs:331) is filled from the tool input. Its only read outside tests is the emptiness check `request.hypothesis.trim().is_empty()` in `ReviewDispatch::validate` (:365). `ReviewDispatch::launch` (:384-388) then turns `requests` into a list of `agent_type` values and drops the rest. So the value never reaches the lane prompt built by `lane_prompt(lane, &self.shared_context, true, ...)` (:427-432), or any log line or return value. The field is checked but never used.
query: Where does the value of the new field `ReviewSubagentRequest::hypothesis` go after deserialization? Does it reach any output (prompt, log, return value, stored state) other than a validity check?
tool_output: src/discrete_review.rs:331: field `hypothesis` (added in this diff) is read only by the emptiness check at :365 in `validate`. Its value never flows to any output. `launch` (:384-388) keeps only `agent_type` and drops the rest of each request. The field is checked but never used.
specificity_reason: Rust's dead-code lint stays silent here because `validate` reads the field. A field whose only read is a validity check, while the containing struct is reduced to one other field, is rare in an ordinary diff. Most new fields reach a prompt, a log line, storage or a computation. The warning names the exact field the lane prompt should contain, so it points straight at the defect. It falls short of a self-lock only because a check-only field is sometimes intended, for example a required confirmation flag.
evidence: I read `git show 9af690d4c0` and src/discrete_review.rs at intro. :325-332 adds `ReviewSubagentRequest` with `hypothesis`, documented as the risk "this lane should investigate". :365 is the emptiness check in `validate`. :384-388 is `requests.into_iter().map(|request| request.agent_type).collect()`. :427-432 builds the prompt with `lane_prompt(lane, &self.shared_context, true, ...)` and no per-request text. `grep hypothesis` at intro finds only :331, :336 (doc), :365/:367 (validate), prompt strings at :1419/:1538/:1649 that tell the supervisor to supply it, and tests at :2370-2409, which check only the schema and validation. All of these lines except :427-432 are in the diff, so the defect is visible there. A tool would still have to state the def-use result out loud.

defect: The rename dialog renders Field focus and Save focus identically, so after tabbing to Save the user cannot see that typing is now ignored.
fact: render_rename_editor (src/hel_tui.rs:6038-6053 at intro) reads editor.focus only through RenameFocus::button_index (src/hel_tui.rs:354-358), which returns 1 for both Field and Save. So the rendered frame is identical for focus == Field and focus == Save. But handle_rename_key and the paste handler branch on focus == RenameFocus::Field (src/hel_tui.rs:1304, 1749, 1755): typing, Backspace and paste edit the title in Field and are dropped in Save. Two states that input handling treats differently draw the same output.
query: Which values of editor.focus can render_rename_editor tell apart, and does input handling branch on a distinction that the render function loses?
tool_output: src/hel_tui.rs:6044: render_rename_editor depends on editor.focus only via button_index(), and button_index maps RenameFocus::Field and RenameFocus::Save to the same value (1). The render output is the same for Field and Save. handle_rename_key (lines 1749, 1755) and paste (line 1304) compare focus == RenameFocus::Field, so these two states behave differently while drawing the same.
specificity_reason: A plain warning that a match arm merges two enum variants would be low: intentional merges are common, and the commit message even defends this one. The useful output joins two facts: the render path cannot tell two variants apart, and the input path branches on exactly that difference. That combination is rarer and points straight at the invisible mode change. Still, a tool would also flag some harmless cases, such as states whose difference does not need to be shown or render functions that leave out internal flags. So the output is something a reviewer would read, but it is not unique to this defect.
evidence: git show 9e6d561405 adds `RenameFocus::Field | RenameFocus::Save => 1` in button_index (src/hel_tui.rs:357 at intro). It rewrites render_rename_editor (6038-6053), which styles the title Cyan without regard to focus and passes editor.focus.button_index() to focused_buttons (6044). It adds Field-only guards on paste (1304), Backspace (1749) and Char (1755). The commit message says Save stays highlighted in both the Field and Save states, so the author chose the merge on purpose for the button row. What the author missed is that nothing else in the render shows which of the two states is active. Everything is in the diff, so I agree with the first pass. A tool would still help by stating that the render cannot tell the two states apart while input handling depends on the difference.

defect: owner_only_create_options binds `let mut options` but only mutates it under #[cfg(unix)], so Windows Clippy with -D warnings fails on unused_mut.
fact: In owner_only_create_options (mj-worker/src/relay/journal.rs:38-46 at intro), the mutable binding `options` declared at line 39 has exactly one mutating use, `options.mode(0o600)` at line 43, and that use is inside `#[cfg(unix)]`. With cfg(unix) false (the Windows target that .github/workflows/windows.yml:41 lints with `-D warnings`), the binding has no mutating use, so rustc's unused_mut lint fires at line 39 and fails the lane.
query: For each `let mut` binding in changed code, under every cfg configuration that CI builds (unix and windows), does the binding have at least one mutating use? Equivalent: run the unused_mut lint for the non-host target too.
tool_output: warning (cfg(not(unix)), target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): variable does not need to be mutable -- mj-worker/src/relay/journal.rs:39 `let mut options`; its only mutation, journal.rs:43 `options.mode(0o600)`, is under #[cfg(unix)]. The Windows CI lane runs clippy with -D warnings (.github/workflows/windows.yml:41), so this is an error there.
specificity_reason: An unused_mut warning under a CI-built cfg is rare in an ordinary diff, and when it appears it is exactly the defect: it names the line and is a guaranteed CI failure, not a neutral fact. The defect is only invisible on Linux because the author's host compiles the cfg(unix) branch; a cross-cfg def-use check or the same compiler lint run for the Windows target states it directly.
evidence: git show f41710c8ca: mj-worker/src/relay/journal.rs:38-46 adds owner_only_create_options with `let mut options = OpenOptions::new();` (line 39), a `#[cfg(unix)] { use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt; options.mode(0o600); }` block (lines 40-44, mutation at 43), then `options`. No other statement mutates it. .github/workflows/windows.yml:41 at intro runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`. The fix a6ee05b7f ("Fix Windows journal creation Clippy warning") makes the outer binding immutable and rebinds `let mut options = options;` inside a `#[cfg(unix)] let options = { ... };` block. The whole function is in the diff hunk, so the defect is visible there. A reviewer has to evaluate the function under the non-Unix cfg in their head; a cross-target lint would state the result outright.

defect: Popup rectangles are added to ordinary reverse-registration hit testing. A later registered field underneath an open dropdown wins over the visually covering popup, activating the wrong control.
fact: In render_review_settings, the open combobox is registered twice in one frame: first collapsed inside the selector loop (mj-tui/src/review_settings.rs:1004), then again after the later selectors and ButtonRow (review_settings.rs:1051) so that its popup is painted last (review_settings.rs:1071). The second call reaches Form::register_combobox, and its `if !self.order.contains(&id) { self.order.push(id) }` (mj-chat/src/components/scope.rs:477-479) does nothing because the id is already in `self.order`. The id therefore keeps its early position. Form::hit (scope.rs:848-858) takes the last entry in `self.order` whose `area` or `popup_area` contains the click. So any selector or button registered after the open combobox wins over the popup that covers it. The paint order and the hit-test order differ.
query: After the second `register_combobox(id, …)` call at review_settings.rs:1071, where is `id` in `form.order`, and which controls come after it, so that `Form::hit` checks them before the popup?
tool_output: mj-tui/src/review_settings.rs:1071: `ComboBox::render(…, id)` → `Form::register_combobox` does not change `self.order`. `id` was already pushed by the earlier call at review_settings.rs:1004 (scope.rs:477 `!self.order.contains(&id)` is false). The order position stays at the first registration. Controls registered after it (later selectors, ButtonRow at review_settings.rs:1051) come first in `Form::hit`'s `order.iter().rev()` scan (scope.rs:852), even though this call sets `popup_area` and paints over them.
specificity_reason: A same-id re-registration whose only intended effect is ordering, where the order effect is skipped, is uncommon: most register calls happen once per id per frame. A tool that reports "this call's push is a no-op because the id is already present" would fire only where a control is registered twice in one frame. That happens in a few places in a form-heavy diff, and here the re-registration exists only to paint last. It is not high because the tool would also report harmless double registrations, and it does not by itself say that hit order should follow paint order. The reviewer still has to connect it to Form::hit's reverse scan.
evidence: git show 8a203905e: scope.rs:454-481 register_combobox (popup_area set at 476, conditional push at 477-479); scope.rs:848-858 Form::hit uses `self.order.iter().rev()` with one predicate over `area || popup_area`; scope.rs:317 clears order each frame. review_settings.rs:982 `expanded_combo`, :1004 collapsed ComboBox::render in the selector loop, :1019 records the open id, :1051 ButtonRow::render, :1070-1084 re-render of the expanded combobox after ButtonRow. controls.rs:475 and :528 show that ComboBox::render calls register_combobox. Fix 20b5749a2 changes only Form::hit to check popup_area across all controls before area, and its commit message says that repainting last did not change the order. All the parts are in the diff, but you have to combine them across two files to see the defect, so a tool that states the no-op re-registration out loud would help.

defect: A metadata-only capture is marked metadata-only only when it contains saved review refs. With no refs, restore takes the full checkout path and can reset a shared working checkout to the archived commit.
fact: The new field `RepositoryMetadata.review_refs_metadata_only` has exactly two writers. `collect_git_metadata_snapshot` sets it to `!saved_refs.is_empty()` (mj-checkpoint/src/archive/git.rs:200), and `collect_git_contents` sets it to `false` (git.rs:1848). So when `collect_review_refs` returns no refs, a metadata-only snapshot holds `false`, the same value as a full-contents snapshot. That snapshot then gets past the new guard at git.rs:1941 with `restore_contents` still true. It reaches `git checkout -B <branch> <head_commit>` at git.rs:2020, or `git checkout --detach` at git.rs:2029, with an empty `committed_bundle`.
query: What values can `review_refs_metadata_only` hold on a snapshot produced by `collect_git_metadata_snapshot`? When it is false there, which code in `restore_git_snapshot_for_session` runs?
tool_output: Annotation on git.rs:200: "`review_refs_metadata_only` is false here when `saved_refs` is empty. Writers of this field: git.rs:200 (`!saved_refs.is_empty()`), git.rs:1848 (`false`). Where it is false, the guard at git.rs:1941 leaves `restore_contents` unchanged. With `committed_bundle` = `Vec::new()` (git.rs:219), restore then runs `git checkout -B branch head_commit` (git.rs:2020)."
specificity_reason: A writer list for a new field is short and a reviewer would read it. In this diff it shows a snapshot kind that claims to be metadata-only but can carry false. Linking that false value to the checkout call outside the diff is the important part. Still, a tool that lists field writers and the branches each value reaches would print similar notes for every new boolean field. It does not single out this case the way a self-lock warning would.
evidence: I read `git show 86494146f` and the file at intro. Line 200 adds `review_refs_metadata_only: !saved_refs.is_empty()` inside `collect_git_metadata_snapshot`, which starts at line 189. Line 219 sets `committed_bundle: Vec::new()`. Line 1848 sets `false` in `collect_git_contents`. Line 1941 adds the guard `restore_contents && !snapshot.metadata.review_refs_metadata_only`, under a comment saying raw snapshots restore ref metadata only. Lines 2010-2029 are outside the diff: `checkout_target = head_commit` when the bundle is empty, then `checkout -B` or `checkout --detach`. The callers are capture.rs:773 (the metadata capture) and restore.rs:266, 375 and 399. Fix 38f041c03 changes line 200 to `true` unconditionally. The defect is visible from the diff, but only because the condition contradicts the commit message. The checkout it lets through is outside the hunks.

defect: All non-prefix label matches share one score tier. Multiple word-start bonuses can make a scattered subsequence outrank a contiguous literal substring, putting Resize pane down above Toggle transcript rendering for rend.
fact: At intro, mj-tui/src/palette.rs:157-160 in match_score sends every label that does not start with the query to one tier, 1_000 + subsequence_score. subsequence_score (palette.rs:167-192) matches each query character at its first occurrence and never backtracks. It adds 30 per word start (palette.rs:177) and 20 per adjacent pair (palette.rs:182). For "rend", "Toggle transcript rendering" matches r inside "transcript" and e,n,d inside "rendering", for 40 points. "Resize pane down" matches R+e at a word start plus adjacency and d at a word start, for 80 points. So a scattered match outranks a label that contains the query as a contiguous run. No tool can call this wrong without knowing the intended ranking. A tool could only print the weights or the computed scores, which is a true but neutral fact.
evidence:
I read `git show 33b58e3c7d` and the intro version of mj-tui/src/palette.rs. match_score is at line 150, and the prefix tier returns 10_000. The subsequence tier at line 160 returns `1_000 + score`, and the description tier returns 100. No branch handles a contiguous substring that is not a prefix. In subsequence_score (line 167), `chars.next()?` at line 174 takes the greedy first occurrence, `score += 30` for a word start is at line 177, and `score += 20` for adjacency is at line 182.

The fix fb0622d0f1 adds a 5_000 tier for `label_lower.find(&query)`. Its commit message calls the problem a ranking choice ("A run of the query in the label is what a reader means by a match"). That is an intended-behavior judgment about scoring weights, not a fact about code structure, so I chose kind none with reason logic.

The closest tool fact would be constant or range analysis showing that word-start bonuses (30) can exceed adjacency bonuses (20). That is the value-flow alternative. It would be neutral without the intended order.

Note: "Resize pane down" does not exist at intro (`git grep` finds no match at 33b58e3c7d). It first appears by fb0622d0f1, at mj-tui/src/actions.rs:562. "Toggle transcript rendering" is at actions.rs:817 at intro. So the scoring logic at intro already contained the defect, but the example that triggers it came from a label added later.

defect: New direct workspace Rename/Close shortcuts open a manager subview, but Escape/Cancel resets that subview to the manager list. The user is taken to a screen absent from the navigation path.
fact: The Rename and Close views of WorkspaceManager now have two entry routes. specificity_reason: A plain list of transitions would be low specificity, because a TUI diff adds many transitions. The narrower output, a new entry into an existing state whose exits return to a predecessor that this entry skips, is uncommon. Here it points at exactly this defect. But the tool cannot know whether returning to List is wrong, since some dialogs do intend a fixed parent. So it would also flag some harmless "back to parent" designs. A reviewer would read it, but it is not as clear-cut as a self-lock.
